job.title: Customer Service Consultant
job.description:
Customer Service Consultant
Kitchen Hardware Showroom
$75k - $80k + Super
UNDERWOOD, QLD - 4119
Permanent - Full-time
On-site role (Monday – Friday 9 – 5 only)

Cox Purtell is currently working with a world-renowned, family-owned global leader in functional furniture fittings, who are seeking a dedicated and customer-focused individual to join their team as a Showroom Consultant. Their products are trusted in kitchens and homes around the world, and as a family-owned company, they place a genuine emphasis on their people, offering real opportunities for career growth and development within a global organisation.

Role Overview:
Reporting to the State Sales Manager, as Showroom Consultant you would plan and deliver marketing and sales activities to grow the product range within their showroom market. It's a great fit for someone with a retail, trade counter or customer service background, perhaps from a hardware, kitchen supply or similar showroom environment, who enjoys a hands-on, customer-facing role.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Customer Support:

  • Responsible for greeting customers and supporting them through their visit at the Showroom.
  • Responsible for answering incoming calls in a timely and professional manner.
  • Responsible for maintaining customer/visitor registration database.
  • Maintain and develop existing and new customers face-to-face through appropriate propositions and ethical sales methods.
  • Where required, support all staff in preparing for customer visits, trade events, or VIP customer visits.
  • Attend and assist in representing the organisation at trade shows, exhibitions and special events as required.
  • Responsible for follow up calls, communications and campaigns as required.

Administrative:

  • Perform general administration duties as required within the role and in a timely fashion (maintaining files, records & documents).
  • Ensure showroom and aligned state is well maintained including:
  • Appearance, cleanliness and hygiene.
  • Working order of displays and equipment.
  • Building maintenance as per lease agreements.
  • Ensure marketing material and brochures are readily available.

Planning:

  • Through internal training and product knowledge, be competent in presenting specific topics to a variety of audiences.
  • Utilise internal program to maintain and develop a computerised customer and prospect database.
  • Assist with new product release campaigns, functions and training programs as required.

Skills & Experience:

  • Well-developed inter-personal skills.
  • Solid organization skills.
  • Ability to work well with others.
  • Problem solving and time management skills.
  • Effective verbal, presentation and listening communications skills.
  • Effective written communications skills.
  • Previous experience/exposure to an internal sales environment particularly in relation to kitchen hardware would be highly regarded.

Why Apply?

  • Be part of a world-renowned, family-owned company with a strong focus on people, quality and values.
  • Work with a dynamic team committed to delivering exceptional customer service.
  • If you're a customer-focused individual with a passion for providing outstanding service and technical support, we want to hear from you! Apply now and become a part of the team.

job.title: Field Sales Representative
job.description:
Sales Representative – Stairlift & Accessibility Solutions

  • Sydney Inner West

  • Strong inbound leads and momentum from day one in a high-growth Sydney and NSW territory

Our client is an established and market-leading business in the lift and accessibility industry, with over 100 years of combined industry experience behind it. They design, manufacture and supply stairlifts, vertical lifts, inclined platform lifts and custom accessibility solutions across Australia. The business continues to grow strongly, driven by innovation, a premium product range and an excellent reputation in the market.

About the Role

As Sales Representative, you will manage and convert a steady pipeline of inbound B2B and B2C sales opportunities across a high-growth territory covering metropolitan Sydney and select areas of NSW. You will conduct in-home appointments and consultative product demonstrations, helping customers understand how the right solution meets their needs, and close high-value sales with confidence and professionalism. This is a role for someone who builds lasting customer relationships through exceptional service while representing a trusted brand in the accessibility and mobility space.

Duties

  • Manage and convert inbound B2B and B2C sales opportunities through to close.
  • Conduct in-home appointments and deliver engaging, high-impact product demonstrations.
  • Take a consultative approach to selling, helping customers understand how solutions meet their needs.
  • Build lasting customer relationships through exceptional service and follow-up.
  • Represent the brand professionally across both business and consumer sales conversations.

Requirements

  • Proven success in an autonomous, high-ticket sales role.
  • Organised and structured, with confidence presenting to both businesses and consumers.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and a genuine focus on customer service.
  • A competitive, results-driven mindset.
  • Interest in, or willingness to build expertise in, accessibility and mobility solutions.
  • Full working rights in Australia, a full driving licence, and your own vehicle

How to Apply

If this sounds like the high-growth sales opportunity you have been looking for, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Operations & Membership Officer
job.description:
Are you an experienced association or B2B professional looking for a role where you can genuinely shape the growth of a peak industry body? My client, a national association representing suppliers of packaging and processing automation, technology and equipment, is looking for an Operations & Membership Officer to help drive their member and industry services forward.

The organisation runs industry-leading events, including a flagship triennial trade exhibition, alongside a strong member services and partnerships program. With over 150 Australian-based company members, this is a genuinely varied role working closely with the General Manager, CEO and business partners across the full operations of the association.

What you'll be doing:

  • Proactively identifying, targeting and converting new member companies to drive satisfaction, retention and growth.
  • Coordinating the association's presence at domestic and international trade events, from stand design and staffing through to marketing and lead follow-up.
  • Building and nurturing relationships with sponsors and service partners, and pitching new partners that resonate with the membership.
  • Driving member communications across newsletters, LinkedIn, forums and other digital channels, including publications and member content.
  • Delivering clear, timely reporting on acquisition, sponsorship revenue, event performance and marketing engagement.
  • Managing the association's recurring events calendar, including its flagship exhibition, an annual awards program, and other member gatherings.

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years' experience in a customer-facing, coordination or business operations role (association, events or B2B environment preferred).
  • Experience in an industry association or membership organisation.
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • High proficiency with CRM/member database systems, MS Office Suite and cloud-based platforms.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a professional context.

Great to have (not essential):

  • Background in events coordination or trade exhibition delivery.
  • Exposure to sponsorship or partnership management.
  • Familiarity with the packaging, processing or broader manufacturing sector.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a relationship-driven operator who wants genuine variety, autonomy and the chance to play a key role in the continued success of a peak industry body.

Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, circa $90,000 to $100,000 plus superannuation, with interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year.

job.title: Senior Dynamics CRM Software Developer
job.description:
Senior Dynamics 365 CRM Developer

Contract | Baseline Clearance Essential | Hybrid | QLD, ACT, VIC or NSW, EL1

Seek selling points

  • Hands-on Dynamics 365 development inside a mature, long-running federal platform
  • Security-cleared work with real technical scope, not just BAU ticket support day to day
  • Hybrid contract open to Developers based in QLD, ACT, VIC or NSW, extension likely

About the client

This is a federal government agency running a genuinely mature, single-vendor Microsoft environment: Dynamics 365, Azure, Power Platform and the full Microsoft 365 stack, all connected rather than bolted together. The Dynamics 365 program itself replaced an ageing legacy CRM and has been embedded, owned and iterated on for years rather than freshly stood up. You will not be walking into a rebuild-from-scratch situation or a vendor sprawl mess. This is a well-funded, stable digital environment with room to do proper engineering.

About the role

As Senior Dynamics 365 CRM Developer, you will build and extend a live Dynamics 365 Customer Service solution used across a multi-disciplinary agile team, working alongside a platform architect and fellow developers rather than in isolation. Your work will span configuration and customisation of D365, extension of Dataverse through the Power Platform, and integration work across the broader Microsoft and Azure estate. You will also carry real responsibility for the security posture of what you ship, not just the functionality. This is a build and problem-solving role for someone who wants technical latitude inside a stable, well-governed program. We will consider candidates based in Queensland, the ACT, Victoria or New South Wales, working in a hybrid arrangement with three days a week in the office.

Duties

  • Provide Dynamics 365 CRM specific technical recommendations as part of the wider solution design.
  • Develop and extend Dynamics 365 solutions, with a particular focus on Customer Service.
  • Perform system analysis, investigate technical problems and document findings clearly.
  • Liaise directly with business users and project stakeholders on both technical and non-technical matters.
  • Work closely with the wider development team, contributing to process and skill improvement.

Requirements

  • Tertiary qualifications in an ICT-related field, or equivalent industry certification.
  • Proven experience as a Microsoft Dynamics 365 solutions developer using .NET Core, C#, JavaScript and TypeScript.
  • Hands-on experience configuring and customising Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
  • Experience extending and automating Dataverse: Power Automate, business process flows and business rules, JavaScript and plugins, Power Apps and Power Pages, Function Apps and Logic Apps, and consuming Web APIs.
  • Solid grasp of secure software development principles and the OWASP Top 10, with the ability to identify, assess and remediate vulnerabilities across applications, integrations and APIs.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, and the ability to communicate clearly at technical, business and personal levels.
  • Must hold, or be eligible for prompt reinstatement of, a Baseline security clearance or above. This is essential, not preferred.
  • Desirable: experience building DevOps build and release pipelines, building web apps with ASP.NET Core and ReactJS, and working within Agile or Scrum teams.
  • Nice to have: exposure to Copilot or AI-assisted features within the Power Platform or Dynamics 365 is a plus given the direction of the wider Microsoft stack, though not required.

How to apply

If this sounds like the kind of technically serious, well-governed environment you want to build in next, we would genuinely like to hear from you. Please apply with a copy of your CV?

job.title: Salesforce Program Manager
job.description:
About the client
A large, Brisbane-based education sector organisation found out the hard way what happens when a Salesforce program runs on status updates instead of delivery. An independent health check surfaced the real state of things: broken data models, access that shouldn't exist, integrations that don't talk to each other, and a backlog of work that was reported as done and wasn't. Salesforce professional services is now on-site for 12 months, and this role builds the internal team that works alongside them to actually fix it.

About the role
This isn't a program manager who flourishes a Gantt chart in a steering committee and calls it leadership. The last person in a seat like this one filled governance forums with noise instead of answers, and the organisation is done with that. You'll be the one who reads a health check and sees a plan, not a crisis. You'll run four workstreams (roadmap and governance, platform foundations, data foundations, strategic use cases), and you'll be judged on whether the platform is actually better in twelve months, not on how polished your reporting deck looked along the way. Two business units pull against each other on a shared platform. You'll need to hold that tension without pretending it isn't there.

Duties

  • Run delivery across all four workstreams to a standard that survives scrutiny, not just a deadline
  • Build governance reporting that tells executives the truth about risk and progress, not a version of it
  • Own the program budget and vendor spend, and know exactly where every dollar is going
  • Earn trust across business units who've been burned before
  • Spot the risks that turn into fires and deal with them before they do

Requirements

  • Real experience leading a Salesforce program through actual complexity, not just scale
  • Multi-cloud depth across Sales, Service, Experience and Marketing Cloud
  • A program or agile delivery certification that backs up the experience (PMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner, SAFe, CSM or PSM II)
  • Financial and vendor management you can defend under questioning
  • The stomach to walk into a program with a documented list of what's wrong and choose to fix it anyway

How to apply
If the words "platform health check" make you want to see the findings, not run from them, we'd like to talk.

job.title: AI Enablement and Innovation Lead
job.description:
AI Enablement & Innovation Lead

Melbourne (Property & Construction) | $180,000 - $190,000 + Super | Full-time, Permanent

  • $180K-$190K + Super, backed by an owner personally obsessed with AI and robotics
  • Real mandate, not theory: agentic workflows already live and running in production
  • Help shape a live SharePoint data foundation, not inherit someone else's legacy mess

About the Client

A well-established Melbourne property and construction business, covering the full pipeline from planning and feasibility through legal, construction, customer experience and post-delivery. Privately owned and ambitious, and already leaning hard into AI: the commitment exists, agentic workflows are live in production, and the owner is personally driving what comes next, not just funding it.

About the Role

Most AI roles ask you to build the case for AI. This one starts after that argument's already been won. You'll take an existing roadmap and turn it into daily capability across the business: rolling out and governing the tools already in use (Claude, Microsoft Copilot), and shaping the SharePoint data foundation currently being built as the business's single source of truth, so it's structured for AI to actually use, not just stored for people to search. You'll run the change management that makes adoption stick, not just launch, and you'll work directly with senior leadership, with real authority to prioritise and ship. And you won't be doing it from a desk: expect to be on site with construction crews as often as you're in the office, because that's where half of this business actually happens.

Duties

  • Extend an AI roadmap that's already live, building on the agentic workflows already in production.
  • Act as the internal evangelist and custodian for AI adoption, driving change management across teams already using generative AI tools day to day.
  • Shape the structure of the business's growing SharePoint data foundation so it's genuinely usable as an AI knowledge source, not just well organised for people.
  • Partner with an external AI consultant and the business's outsourced IT provider to prioritise, build and embed new use cases.
  • Get on site with construction crews regularly, understanding real workflows before automating them.

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience deploying and governing generative or agentic AI tools inside a real business, not just advising on them from outside.
  • Understanding of how SharePoint content and data structure needs to change to support AI grounding, not just document governance and permissions.
  • A track record of driving change management and adoption, not just technology rollout.
  • Confidence operating autonomously alongside senior leadership and external consultants, without needing constant direction.
  • Genuinely willing to work in the office five days a week and get on site: this role trades remote flexibility for a seat at the table and a business that actually acts on what you build.

How to Apply

If you want to build AI capability somewhere that's already committed, not somewhere still deciding, we'd like to hear from you.

job.title: Lead Observability Platform Engineer
job.description:
Observability Platform Engineer

Sydney | Full-time

Seek Selling Points

  • You already know when the telemetry is lying before the dashboard ever admits it
  • Attractive salary, real bonus, and a rewards package built for someone this good
  • High-frequency, low-latency, mission-critical work, built for genuinely serious minds

About the Client

You'll be joining an organisation operating at the sharp end of technology: high-frequency, high-throughput, low-latency systems where speed, precision and reliability aren't aspirations, they're the job. Here, downtime or delay has a real, measurable cost, not just reputational noise. It's the kind of environment that suits people who've worked across high-stakes sectors, from finance, trading and gaming through to telecommunications and mission-critical government and defence technology, and who already know the difference between a system that's fast and one that's actually trustworthy. Sydney based, corporate, well-resourced, and built for people who want the hardest version of this job, not the easiest.

About the Role

You're the one who gets pulled into the incident channel first, not last. You've already built or fixed the observability platform other engineers rely on without thinking about it, and you know that's the whole point: it should be invisible until the moment it isn't. This role puts you in charge of that platform end to end, metrics, logs, traces, events, alerting and diagnostics, the layer that tells everyone else what's actually happening under load. You already treat observability as a trust problem, not a tooling problem. That instinct is exactly why this role exists.

Duties

  • You'll design, build and operate a shared observability platform spanning telemetry collection, ingestion, storage, query, visualisation, alerting and diagnostics.
  • You'll build the services, APIs, integrations and dashboards that make observability easier to adopt and more reliable to operate.
  • You'll improve the scalability, reliability, performance and cost-effectiveness of high-volume telemetry systems.
  • You'll improve developer and operator experience through self-service workflows, golden paths and practical platform abstractions.
  • You'll own the reliability of what you build, including failure modes, monitoring, incident learnings and continuous improvement.

Requirements

  • You've got strong engineering experience in SRE, platform engineering, infrastructure, observability, developer tooling or distributed systems.
  • You already reason about failure modes, debugging workflows and service reliability under pressure, because you've had to.
  • You have technical depth across logs, metrics, traces, events, alerting, dashboards and telemetry pipelines, not just familiarity.
  • You've designed, built or operated services, pipelines or tools that other engineering teams depend on.
  • You're comfortable with modern observability and telemetry tooling across metrics, logging, tracing and time-series systems, and you keep up with where it's heading.

How to Apply

If most of this reads like a description of how you already work, not what you're hoping to grow into, we should talk.

job.title: AEM Customer Success Manager
job.description:
AEM Customer Success Manager

About the client

Our client is a global software company whose digital experience products sit behind some of the most recognisable brands and websites in the world. Their APAC Customer Success team works with a large enterprise portfolio, helping organisations get genuine commercial return from significant technology investments. The culture is collaborative, data-informed and genuinely customer-obsessed, with the scale and structure you would expect from a major multinational and the autonomy to shape how you work. This is a permanent role based in Sydney CBD with hybrid working.

About the role

As a Solutions Customer Success Manager you will act as the trusted advisor across a portfolio of enterprise customers, working in a dynamic one-to-many model through fixed-scope engagements. Your focus is adoption and value: quickly pinpointing where a customer is underusing their solutions, running the engagement that closes that gap, and evidencing the outcome in a value summary co-owned with your stakeholders. You will work across the enterprise book of business to reach the customers who need help most, ideally before they know they need it. It is a role for someone who enjoys deep product expertise, commercial conversations and the pace of moving between engagements rather than sitting on a single account.

Duties

      • Own overall customer success across an enterprise portfolio, driving feature adoption, improving customer health and evidencing confirmed value delivered.
      • Scope and deliver fixed-timeframe engagements, identifying specific areas of improvement and executing against them within the agreed scope.
      • Align engagement outcomes to value summaries co-owned with key customer stakeholders, so customer value and commercial value move together.
      • Run customer workshops and advisory sessions that showcase best practice and new ways to extend digital maturity across the product suite.
      • Analyse adoption data and customer feedback to spot patterns, recommend improvements and surface areas of unmet demand, then feed that intelligence back internally as the voice of the customer.

Requirements

      • Five or more years of relevant experience, ideally across digital or experience marketing, content management or customer journey management.
      • Two or more years of hands-on solution expertise with Adobe Technology in AEM sites and AEM assets including EDS.
      • Background in a large SaaS environment or another major multinational, working with enterprise-scale customers.
      • Working knowledge of AI and agent capabilities, with content supply chain and modern delivery architecture exposure highly regarded.
      • Proven track record as a trusted advisor, translating product capability into business ROI and measurable customer value.
      • Consulting or business consulting experience, with the commercial mindset to hold value conversations at a senior level.
      • Strong stakeholder and interpersonal skills, including the ability to navigate and mediate conflict and build durable partnerships.
      • Ability to prioritise across multiple concurrent engagements and perform effectively under pressure.
      • Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
      • Flexibility to travel approximately 20% of the time.
      • Bachelor's or master's degree.
      • Full Australian working rights.

How to apply

If this sounds like the next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply with an up to date CV for immediate consideration.

job.title: Accountant
job.description:
Project Accountant
Full-time permanent role
Redfern (WFH flexibility) | Full time | $90,000–$100,000 + super

  • Redfern with genuine work-from-home flexibility offered
  • Own end-to-end project finance for a fast-growing creative agency across Sydney and APAC
  • Hands-on, varied role offering real autonomy and close exposure to production teams daily

About the client

Our client is a dynamic, fast-growing agency with a well-established presence across the Asia-Pacific region, including offices in Sydney and Singapore. Known for delivering high-quality creative and production work for a diverse portfolio of clients, the business has built a reputation for commercial rigour paired with a genuinely collaborative culture. Finance sits close to the action here, partnering directly with Producers and Account Leads rather than operating at arm's length. It is a business that values precision, integrity and strong working relationships as much as the numbers themselves.

About the role

This is a hands-on, commercially focused role for a Project Accountant ready to take ownership of the full financial lifecycle of projects, from revenue recognition and billing through to job costing and final reconciliations. Reporting to the APAC Controller and working closely with Producers and Account Leads, you will become the financial backbone behind projects delivered across Sydney and Singapore. Based in Redfern with the flexibility to work from home, this role offers genuine variety, autonomy and the opportunity to make a visible commercial impact within a close-knit, supportive finance team.

Duties

  • Own project job costing, setting up vendors and maintaining accurate project costs across operating and finance systems.
  • Review and match purchase orders and vendor invoices against project budgets and deliverables, monitoring PO closures ahead of final reconciliation.
  • Manage vendor and freelancer onboarding and compliance across the APAC region, including Certificates of Insurance, Master Service Agreements, rate cards and Scopes of Work.
  • Oversee the APAC accounts payable and receivable function, including invoice processing, aging management, weekly payment runs and supplier reconciliations.
  • Support month-end close by performing bank reconciliations, processing general journals and assisting with GL reconciliations.

Requirements

  • Accounting degree or equivalent qualification.
  • 3–5 years' accounting experience, ideally with a focus on agency finance or project accounting.
  • Strong Excel skills and proficiency with accounting software; experience with Procim is highly regarded.
  • Solid understanding of GST compliance requirements across Australia and Singapore.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with a demonstrated ability to build strong relationships with producers, account managers and external vendors.
  • A self-motivated, proactive problem solver comfortable prioritising across multiple projects and dynamic teams.

How to apply

If you're a commercially minded accountant who thrives on ownership, variety and being close to the action, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Associate Sales Operation Analyst
job.description:
Associate Sales Operations Analyst

12-Month Contract | $99,000 + Super | Sydney, Hybrid

We're partnering with a Fortune 500 client, a large, well-established global technology company with a strong presence across the enterprise software sector, to find an Associate Sales Operations Analyst for a 12-month, Sydney-based hybrid contract. They offer a collaborative, data-driven environment with genuine exposure to senior stakeholders and global systems.

About the role

As Associate Sales Operations Analyst, you'll own coverage, ramp and CRM data for your assigned region, working closely with BDR leadership to keep territory planning accurate and actionable. You'll translate data such as attainment trends, ARR movement and close-date shifts into clear insights that inform staffing, coverage and capacity decisions, partnering closely with senior stakeholders along the way.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own coverage, ramp and CRM hygiene data for the assigned region, acting as the primary point of contact for these datasets.
  • Build and maintain attainment reporting for BDR leadership cadences, translating territory-level signals into inputs for the global capacity model.
  • Run recurring diagnostic checks, including weekly ARR and close-date movement analysis, escalating and acting on anomalies as they arise.
  • Maintain territory assignments and headcount status, proactively flagging coverage gaps and staffing needs to the Capacity and Annual Planning Manager.
  • Partner with regional BDR leaders on territory planning questions, data requests and broader operational improvements.

Requirements

  • 1 to 3 years of experience in Sales Operations, Sales Strategy, Marketing Operations, Go-to-Market or a related function, ideally within the software industry.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, finance or a related field.
  • Strong data analysis skills across Excel, SQL, Tableau or similar tools.
  • Working knowledge of CRM platforms such as Salesforce or Dynamics, plus tools like Outreach.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills; experience with Power BI is an advantage.
  • Strong attention to detail and a genuine commitment to data accuracy.
  • Comfort working with planning, coverage and staffing models, and translating data into actionable business insights.

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
Retail Operations Manager | QSR Industry | Premium Brand
Sydney | Full-time, Permanent
Salary depending on experience, $90-120k+

  • Step into a leadership role, not a turnaround, with a proven, reliable team in place

  • Demonstrated experience in labour planning, cost control and delivering against commercial targets.
  • Working knowledge of food safety and WHS compliance obligations in a retail or hospitality setting.
  • Experience coaching, developing and supporting store managers or team leaders.
  • Comfortable working a rotating roster that includes one weekend in every two.
  • Strong personal presentation and customer experience focus suited to a premium, brand-led environment.

job.title: Customer Success Lead - Digital
job.description:
Customer/Digital Success Lead - iMIS
Melbourne, Hybrid | Open to Sydney, Adelaide or Brisbane
Permanent full-time, package depending on experience

A specialist technology consultancy working exclusively with membership organisations, associations and unions is looking for an experienced Digital Success Lead to join their growing Australian team. With a client base of 150+ organisations across Australia and globally, and partnerships with leading platforms including iMIS, Salesforce and Fonteva, this is a business that helps membership organisations reduce digital transformation risk, align technology with strategy and make their systems work in practice.

This is a rare opportunity for an experienced NFP or associations professional with deep iMIS expertise to move into a solution leadership role, owning the alignment between a client's investment objectives and the system being delivered.

About the Role

This is not a technical delivery role. It is a relationship-led, solution leadership position for someone who deeply understands how membership organisations and associations operate, and can hold a client and delivery team to that understanding throughout an implementation.

As Digital Success Lead, you will own the alignment between the client's investment objectives and the solution being delivered. You will ensure the implementation exploits iMIS's native capability, drive operational change over customisation, and establish the foundation for the client's ongoing Digital Success program.

About You

  • 8+ years in enterprise or membership-system implementations, with deep functional command of iMIS, including demonstrated experience leading a complete implementation lifecycle from discovery through go-live, not limited to configuration, support or add-on module work
  • Previous experience working within an association, member-based organisation or NFP is essential
  • Certified iMIS Professional (CIP) or equivalent highly regarded
  • Demonstrated ability to influence executives and push back on delivery teams, without owning day-to-day project management duties
  • Business-process and change-management fluency, comfortable measuring adoption and value realisation
  • A natural communicator who can engage and influence at a senior level
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex requirements into clear solutions
  • Self-driven, proactive and comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy

Why This Role

  • Join a genuinely specialist consultancy with deep expertise in a sector you already know and care about
  • Work with a global team of straight-talking specialists across Australia, the UK and Europe
  • Trusted by over 150 organisations worldwide across the associations, unions and NFP sector
  • Flexible hybrid working, Melbourne-based with options considered in Sydney, Adelaide or Brisbane
  • A collaborative, values-led business with a strong reputation and a growing Australian client base

If you have built your career in the associations or NFP sector, know iMIS inside out, and are ready to move from delivery into solution leadership, we would love to hear from you.
